extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of 19th-century exploration / natural-history travel narratives; naval surveyors; creative writers studying voyage prose
extracted.subtask_description: Compose detailed voyage/travel accounts that combine precise nautical surveying, natural-history observation, place-naming and moral/ethnographic commentary; suitable for ship logs, published voyage narratives, and creative recreations of exploration writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise navigational detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Record bearings, distances, and coordinates when describing positions (e.g., 'bearing North 76 degrees West (true) twelve miles and a quarter from Fremantle gaol'; 'latitude 28 degrees 58 minutes 26 seconds South and longitude 1 degree 47 minutes 32 seconds west of Swan River').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact compass bearings, distances, latitude and longitude to establish location and authority. Include references to local meridians or anchor points (the text notes referring longitudes to 'Scott's Jetty, Swan River'). Precise data supports reproducibility and usefulness for navigation or scientific follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundings and seabed description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed depth measurements and bottom character (fathoms, sand/rock/mud) and report abrupt shoaling (e.g., 'seven or eight fathoms, on sandy mud... a quarter of a mile nearer the shore the bottom shoals rapidly to four and three fathoms, on rocky ground').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both numeric soundings and qualitative seabed notes. Note gradients and sudden shoals since these affect anchoring safety. Use soundings to infer banks and submerged features and explain hazards encountered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchorage description and safety advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe anchorage position, shelter bearings, suitable depth and seasonal safety (e.g., 'proper berth... in seven or eight fathoms, on sandy mud, about a mile from the gaol'; 'can only be considered safe in the summer season').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the berth coordinates, safe wind directions, bottom type, and reasons why wrecks occur when improper berths are chosen. Explain practical consequences (dragging anchor, exposure while discharging cargo) to advise future mariners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Botanical cataloguing in tabular form
rubrics_metrics.description: Present plant information in systematic columns: 'NAME COMMONLY GIVEN BY SETTLERS / NATIVE NAME / GENUS / REMARKS' (e.g., entries for 'Mahogany : Jarrail* : Eucalyptus : Grows on white sandy land').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear tabular scheme: settler/common name, indigenous name, scientific genus, and habitat/remarks. This enables both scientific usefulness and cultural documentation; include pronunciation footnotes where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record indigenous names and pronunciation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include native names for species and places and annotate pronunciation (e.g., footnote: 'The letter a is sounded broad and full as in Father.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcribe local/indigenous names alongside common/scientific names and give pronunciation guidance or footnotes to preserve linguistic detail and respect source usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnographic and moral reflection on indigenous peoples
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextualize behaviour and punishment of indigenous people with historical injustice and recommend humane treatment (e.g., 'Many... are in some measure unconscious of guilt; and they are almost incapable of appreciating the relation between what they have committed and the punishment which has fallen on them... induce him to judge more leniently... resort to the means... of raising the despised and oppressed savage more nearly to a level with himself').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing indigenous peoples, include causes of dispossession, moral judgments about policy, and advocacy for humane measures rather than mere coercion. Use empathic observation to counter prevailing mistreatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine quantitative scientific data with qualitative observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interleave measurements (e.g., 'tide rose here 32 inches', 'Mount Fairfax proving to be 585 feet, and Wizard Peak 700 feet') with descriptive commentary on appearance and utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance numeric detail (elevations, tides, fathoms) with descriptive context to make data meaningful; this mixture supports both scientific and literary aims and establishes credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-history description of fauna with behavioral notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe animals, abundance, behaviour and captive anecdotes (e.g., 'a very pretty lizard... with its tail covered with spines... The Abrolhos lizard is very docile... will eat and drink out of her hand... It changes its skin twice a year').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record species' appearance, habits, abundance, and any interactions with humans (captivity notes, diet). Anecdotal behavioral details enrich natural-history accounts and aid identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological and coral-formation detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Report strata, coral types, wall composition and bathymetric relationships (e.g., 'The upper 20 feet are formed of a peculiar kind of coral, growing in the shape of huge fans... the lower 34 feet of the wall is of the common large branch kind').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the vertical and lateral structure of reefs and rocks, note coral morphologies and depths, and infer larger geomorphological patterns (e.g., shelving off to no bottom with 250 fathoms). Such detail informs geology and reef ecology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toponymy and naming rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain reasons behind place names (e.g., 'we named our temporary anchorage Batavia Road... the whole group Pelsart Group' ; 'Good Friday Harbour... to commemorate the season of the Christian year').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When naming features, state the etymology or commemorative reason; this provides historical context and aids later users in understanding names' origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report archaeological / wreck evidence with artifacts and dating
rubrics_metrics.description: Document finds such as guns, bottles, coins and their dates and draw inferences (e.g., 'a small brass four-pounder... quantities of ornamental brasswork... two Dutch doits, bearing date 1707 and 1720' and discussion linking to the Zeewyk wreck).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record artifact types, inscriptions/dates, and spatial context; compare with historical records to hypothesize wreck identity. Provide museum deposition information where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological observation and its influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe weather patterns, dramatic phenomena and effects on sea and currents (e.g., 'The winds since the 29th had been very easterly... a stagnant suspicious calm... gale commenced in earnest... current during this breeze set a mile and a half East-South-East').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note wind directions, barometer behavior, squalls, water-spouts, and how air movements influence currents. Use vivid language for dramatic events (singular sunset, heavy gale) while giving practical data (directions, durations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-survey methodology and small-craft operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe boat operations and survey techniques (e.g., 'we hauled a boat to examine the opposite side of the lagoon', 'we passed close round the reef... sounding over by a boat', 'the boats were despatched on their ordinary work').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how surveys were conducted: use of boats for sounding and landing, hauling boats over necks, use of masthead for observation. Include technique and sequence to make methodology reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative analogy to contextualize landscapes
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate unfamiliar features to known ones for reader comprehension (e.g., 'I was forcibly struck with the resemblance between Moresby's Range, Sea Range on the Victoria, Cape Flattery... the cliffs forming the coast range at the head of the Australian Bight').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw analogies to better-known landscapes or previously published descriptions to help readers visualize geography and to argue for broader geological patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: State limitations, uncertainties and cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge missing information, approximations or reliance on others' reports (e.g., 'It was impossible for us to determine... as no account of them had been left with the Surveyor-general, Mr. Roe.'; footnote about approximate longitude).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about where measurements are approximate, where prior charts differ, and cite other voyages or volumes; this honesty helps future investigators assess reliability.
